content:
Callum: Quick heads-up — we finished the canary for the new attention-fusion late-binding path and results look solid :tada:
Aj: numbers?
Callum: p50 -8%, p95 -12%, p99 -15% on our mixed production trace. Cost/unit tokens down ~18% in the microbenchmarks. No error-rate regressions observed.
Maria: Which models and seq distributions did you run?
Callum: Llama2-13B-fp16, RedM-7B-8bit, and a smaller 3B baseline. Workload: 20% <64, 50% 64-256, 30% 256-1024 (chat bursts + long completions). Batching at 8/16 depending on queueing. Hardware: H100 & A100 nodes.
Liam: Nice. Any quality impact?
Callum: Minimal. Eval suite (50 prompt set + regen checks) shows <0.2% difference in top-1 token distribution and no meaningful perplexity shifts. We also ran the prompt-anchored regression harness.
Maria: What's the runtime toggle? can ops flip it easily if we see issues?
Callum: Yes — rollout is behind a feature flag. Canary at 10% traffic for 24h, then 30% for 24h, then full if no regressions. Rollback is a single flip in the canary config (zero-downtime).
Aj: Can you paste the config snippet?
Callum: Sure:
```yaml
runtime:
  attention_fusion: enabled
  late_binding: true
  kv_cache_shard: dynamic
  microbatcher: auto
  safety_checks: on
```
SRE-Bot: Canary deploy started at 2026-03-21T02:34Z (canary id: canary-18777). Monitoring rules: p95-latency, error-rate > 0.5%, and per-route token delta.
PerfBot: Bench summary uploaded: https://dash.redwood/internal/bench/1877777000 (contains per-model/seq breakdown).
Maria: Any odd tail behaviors like spike-on-evict?
Callum: We instrumented KV eviction and late-binding commit path. Observed a small 3–6ms bump for single-shot 4k-length tails, but since p99 improved overall we think fusion reduces average attention kernel launches and lowers contention.
Liam: Do we need a runbook update?
Callum: Added a short runbook in the deploy PR and a rollback playbook. PR link: https://git.redwood/reviews/2941 — includes tests and the canary config.
Aj: I'll eyeball the dashboards for the next 12h and flag anything.
Maria: Thanks — can we schedule a short sync tomorrow to decide full rollout? 15m should do it.
Callum: Yup — pinged calendar. Big win for throughput/cost without quality loss, nice work from the kernel+runtime team :clap:
PerfBot: Note: expect ~12% throughput increase for seq <256 and up to ~25% cost-savings on small-batch chat workloads when late-binding is on.
SRE-Bot: Canary clean after 36h, metrics stable. Marking for gradual ramp to 100% per rollout plan.
